title: do-while Loops
learningObjectives: Explain do-while loops and their execution flow.
Trace condition checks and state changes across iterations.
Select a suitable loop structure for a given problem.
Identify common termination and boundary mistakes.
Apply the loop pattern in an original small program.

understand.concept: do-while executes the body before testing the condition, guaranteeing at least one pass. It ends with a semicolon.
understand.whyItMatters: Menus and prompts often need to display once before the user chooses whether to repeat.
understand.explain: Trace body → condition → repeat or exit. Remember the trailing semicolon.

examples.title: Menu repeat
examples.code: int choice;\ndo { std::cout<<\"1 Start, 0 Exit: \"; std::cin>>choice; } while(choice!=0);
examples.explanation: The prompt occurs at least once.

examples.title: Require positive number
examples.explanation: The first input is read before the condition.

examples.title: Confirmation prompt
examples.explanation: Repeats while the user answers yes.

examples.title: One pass guaranteed
examples.explanation: The body executes once before the condition is checked.

practise.guidedTask: Trace and annotate each of the five do-while Loops examples. For every iteration, record the relevant variable values, condition result and action. Change one input or bound and predict the new behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a small C++ program demonstrating do-while loops in a practical scenario. Include at least three typical tests, two boundary tests, and one invalid or termination test. Explain how the loop terminates.
hints: Place the first required action inside the body.
Evaluate the condition only after the first pass.
Test both repeat and exit responses.
Guard input errors and invalid values.

questions.explanation: The condition is checked after the body.
Menu displays before the repeat decision.

questions.prompt: First pass changes condition to false?
questions.explanation: It checks the condition after first execution.
